A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, algorithm, and Appendices A–C are readable and matchable, including the renaming from Weighted Point Cloud Embedding to Weighted Point Set Embedding.

before.justification: v2 reports original CC3M and CC12M pretraining experiments, zero-shot and linear classification on 13 benchmarks, and component ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original classification experiments, revises their results, and adds CC12M ablation results in Appendix A.4.

M1.justification: The weighted representations, mixed-kernel similarity, random Fourier feature approximation, symmetric InfoNCE objective, and Algorithm 1 remain the same. WPCE becomes WPSE; the expanded padding-token description clarifies an existing component rather than establishing an architectural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use CC3M and CC12M for pretraining and the same 13 classification benchmarks for zero-shot and linear evaluation. The new CC12M ablation reuses existing dataset and task coverage.

E2.justification: CLIP remains the external baseline in Tables 1 and 2. New Table 6 compares the CC12M mixed-kernel model against WPSE Linear and WPSE Nonlinear, adding a quantitative nonlinear-only comparator beyond v2's tabulated CC3M variants.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 expands the reported mixture-coefficient search from four choices for CC3M and three for CC12M to five for both: (0.667, 0.333) is added for both, and (0.6, 0.4) for CC12M. Appendix A.4 adds CC12M component controls. Existing splits, metrics, model sizes, training epochs, and RFF dimensions remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix A.4 and Table 6 extend the kernel-component analysis to CC12M, comparing mixed, linear-only, and nonlinear-only similarities. v3 also specifies a CC3M nonlinear-only NaN failure and adds a CC12M positive-weight NaN failure; v2 already discussed preliminary nonlinear-only training difficulties.

E5.justification: Both versions report five zero-shot evaluations varying RFF randomness, with means in Table 1 and standard deviations in Table 5. Both use one fixed RFF setting for linear evaluation. Updated means and standard deviations do not change the statistical reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1, 2, 3, and 5 substantially revise proposed-model results while retaining CLIP scores. For CC3M pretraining, Gaussian mean linear accuracy changes from 65.88% to 69.01%, reversing its ranking against CLIP at 67.00%. New Table 6 reports mixed/nonlinear-only/linear-only averages of 46.12/44.05/45.87 for zero-shot and 79.08/70.99/78.61 for linear classification. The expanded search limits interpreting cross-version numerical increases as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: The theoretical assumptions, guarantees, and proof arguments are retained. v3 repairs malformed KL-divergence typesetting in Equation (3), restores an omitted gradient symbol in Equation (11), and standardizes probability notation. The corresponding mathematical reasoning was already present in v2.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: richer weighted representations, PMI optimality for symmetric InfoNCE, downstream excess-risk guarantees, approximation capability, and empirical benefits over CLIP. Renaming and additional supporting results do not alter their scope.

C2.justification: Section 5.3 newly explains the tradeoff between RFF approximation variance and inference computation or memory when changing feature dimension. Appendix A.4 adds the interpretation that combining linear and nonlinear kernels benefits both evaluated classification modes on CC12M.

D1.justification: The new Reproducibility Statement announces a code release and supplies an access address absent from v2. Section 5.3 explicitly describes separate padding tokens and independently initialized learnable embeddings. Appendix A's existing architecture and training details are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4.1 broadens attribution of the PMI-optimality observation from Zhang et al. (2023) to include Oord et al. (2018). Related-work positioning otherwise remains stable; bibliography changes mainly standardize metadata, including the existing Vision Transformer reference.

P1.justification: v3 consistently renames point clouds/WPCE to point sets/WPSE, updates the publication header, adds ethics and reproducibility statements, revises appendix headings, and clarifies several passages and notation. The main section order and narrative remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Table 6, moves Table 2 alongside Table 1 on page 9, updates terminology in Figures 1 and 2 and their captions, and reformats equations and page breaks. Existing diagrams and table structures are otherwise retained.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful CC12M evidence separating the kernel components, clarifies padding implementation, and supplies code-access information. It also resolves v2's disagreement between Tables 1 and 5 for CC12M CIFAR-10 results. These provide limited improvements in evidential support, consistency, and reproducibility guidance. The revised accuracies accompany broader hyperparameter searches, so higher scores alone do not establish the improvement.
